scope: Local architecture and recoverability hardening; no IPC deployment, CAN mutation, camera access, Thor request or robot motion.
implemented: Policy and planner failures invalidate epochs and HOLD without promoting network faults to SDK FAULT; explicit independent reload only, no automatic movement.
Planner timeout discards old process/pipe; replay retains submitted gripper targets; shared epoch/time validation.
Task changes and recorder recovery share a paused control barrier; disk/process work stays on background workers; cancellation prevents late writer installation.
Recorder recovery retains failed session, creates a fresh data session; candidate initialization failure preserves original error.
HIL recording failure allows explicit end-intervention to HOLD/teleop before data recovery.
Camera startup/close failures retain cleanup ownership; explicit close retry, no resource stacking; no permanent connecting/disconnecting on Thread.start/import failure.
Per-CAN-channel cooperative cross-process ownership for SDK, bring-up/reset/down; uncertain SDK construction retains ownership until owner exit.
Executor HOLD retains lease, detach revokes lease, session cleanup does not down executor-owned CAN.
Dataset Jobs extracted from Web; broken worker and submit errors release bounded capacity; next explicit submission recreates worker.
Spool and readable segments recovered into a new episode with original tick/time deduplication; sources unchanged, malformed files reported.
Optional system-disk runtime deployment templates and recording mount/device/free-space preflight; Web no longer Requires device service.
Wheel includes all three UIs and ABC schema; current architecture/quickstart corrected and historical architecture archived.

limitations: Default yam-device still owns SDK. Optional persistent executor and system-disk runtime have not migrated to IPC; first deployment requires supported arms and explicit approval.

Mount preflight is a snapshot; require nonwritable underlying mount directory and normal I/O failure handling. New device sessions currently still initialize recording metadata, so strict missing-data-mount policy also refuses new device connection.
